solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pair winning almost immediately?

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of it, so the final letter of the phrase is cut off

parts.note: PR is the standard abbreviation for pair
on top means ahead, winning

explanation.surface: A doubles pair seem to be winning almost straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: Pronto is borrowed from Italian and Spanish, where it means quickly; the question mark covers the informal register.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronto is an informal adverb meaning promptly or at once, a colloquial synonym of immediately.

clue.text: Publicity bod hurried round about and was successful

parts.note: a PRO is a public relations officer

indicators.note: going round something encloses it, so the word for hurried wraps the next piece

parts.note: sped means rushed, hurried
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A publicity agent rushed about the place and made a success of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' works twice over: it turns 'about' backwards and also wraps 'hurried' around the result.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosper is to thrive or do well, so prospered matches was successful as a past-tense verb phrase.

clue.text: Series of deliveries managed but took too long

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled
ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: A bowler got through his set of balls but took longer than allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket: an over is a sequence of six balls delivered by one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that overran went beyond its allotted time, so it took too long.

clue.text: Table with a flower still to be put up outside

indicators.note: being outside something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps the others
in a down clue putting up means turning upwards, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: yet means still, as in still to come
taken as written
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Po is Italy's longest

explanation.surface: A table with a flower arrangement that has still to be set up.
explanation.walkthrough: Flower is the crossword river, something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: A teapoy is a small three-legged table, often used for holding a tea caddy.

clue.text: Married woman or country boy featured in curse

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for married
Alison is a woman's name
an alternative route to the same letters: Mali is an African country and a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A married woman or a lad from the country is caught up in a curse.
explanation.walkthrough: Unusually, the clue offers two complete routes to the same word, joined by 'or': M plus ALISON, or MALI plus SON. Either alone is enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Malison is an archaic word for a curse, the opposite of benison, a blessing.

clue.text: Fellow consuming cold mineral

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so the fellow word takes the other inside

parts.note: a male is a man, a fellow
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A man drinking something cold and full of minerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Macle is a name for chiastolite, a mineral, or a twinned crystal.

clue.text: Solitary advance amount of cash reported

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the phrase counts for how it sounds

parts.note: a loan is an advance of money, and a sum is an amount

explanation.surface: A single cash advance gets mentioned in a report.
explanation.definitionFit: Lonesome describes someone alone and lonely, close to solitary in sense.

clue.text: Bird with leg in something mouldy

parts.note: a stilt is a long-legged wading bird
in cricket leg and on name the same side of the field

explanation.surface: A wading bird stands with one leg in some mouldy muck.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket: the leg side is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilton is an English blue cheese veined with edible mould, so it is something mouldy.

clue.text: Country boy with change of direction finally

indicators.note: a switch of direction at the end swaps one compass or side letter for its opposite in the last place

parts.note: Nigel is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A boy from the country finally changes direction.
explanation.walkthrough: Left becomes right: the closing L turns into R.
explanation.definitionFit: Niger is a landlocked country in West Africa.

clue.text: Bishop back, having embraced the brief time out?

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so the back word encloses the next

parts.note: the rear is the back
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bishop returns after embracing the brief, perhaps a lawyer needing a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like a lawyer, the noun; it belongs to the definition as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A breather is a short rest or pause, a brief break from activity.

clue.text: Old piano delivered before time for stage performance

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
p is the musical marking for piano, softly
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: An old piano is delivered just before a show goes on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a dramatic work set to music and performed on a stage, so it is a kind of stage performance.

clue.text: Forswearing group full of English hypocrisy

indicators.note: something full of other things holds them inside it, so the group word wraps round the rest

parts.note: a ring is a group or gang, as in a spy ring
E is the abbreviation for English
cant is insincere, hypocritical talk

explanation.surface: A gang that is thoroughly English and hypocritical gives up its old vows.
explanation.definitionFit: To recant is to withdraw a statement or belief formally, which is to forswear it; both are present participles here.

clue.text: A boy given time becomes VIP

parts.note: per means a or each, as in fifty miles per hour
a son is a boy
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A lad who is given enough time grows up into a very important person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' looks like the article but stands for per, as in 'twice a day'.
explanation.definitionFit: A personage is a person of rank or distinction, much the same as a very important person.

clue.text: Instrument costing nothing no good? Return it!

indicators.note: returning something sends it back the way it came, so the letters are read backwards
no here means without, so the letters for good are removed

parts.note: gratis means free, costing nothing
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A free instrument that turns out to be no good should be sent back.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitar is a long-necked Indian stringed instrument, a specific example of a musical instrument.

clue.text: Payment slashed?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: money paid regularly for the use of a property
second meaning: torn apart, the past participle of rend

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a payment being cut; the second sense is the old past tense of rend, to tear.
explanation.definitionFit: Rent is both the sum a tenant pays a landlord and an adjective meaning torn or split open.

clue.text: Remarkable chum hugging female and old blokes

indicators.note: to hug is to wrap arms round, so the friend word encloses the others

parts.note: a pal is a chum, a friend
a hen is a female bird
O is the abbreviation for old
blokes are men in British slang

explanation.surface: A remarkable friend who hugs both a woman and some old fellows.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomenal means extraordinary or exceptional, so it is a strong synonym of remarkable.

clue.text: Ignore heartless nut spouting gas

indicators.note: spouting suggests letters gushing out in a jumble, so they are rearranged
heartless means with the centre removed, so the middle letter goes

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, before its middle letter is removed

explanation.surface: Pay no attention to the brainless lunatic spouting hot air.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrogen is the colourless gas making up most of the atmosphere, an example of a gas.

clue.text: Heather coming across snake and running

indicators.note: coming across can mean spanning over, so the heather word stretches round the other

parts.note: ling is a common heather
the adder is Britain's venomous snake

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles across a snake in the heather and runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' is not sprinting but what happens to tights when a thread breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tights are laddering when a run spreads up them, so laddering means running in the hosiery sense.

clue.text: A revolutionary socialist restricts fair person who'd make small changes

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: restricting something hems it in, so the reversed word encloses the next
a revolution turns things round, so the next word is read backwards

parts.note: a red is a left-winger, a socialist
just means fair, equitable

explanation.surface: A radical left-winger keeps a fair-minded reformer in check.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjuster tweaks or fine-tunes things, someone who makes slight alterations.

clue.text: Trade ad is out to catch people ultimately, offering essential items?

indicators.note: catching something takes it in, so the shuffled letters close round one more
out suggests the words are put out of order and rearranged

parts.note: nine letters taken as written for rearranging

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of people

explanation.surface: A trade advert sets out to hook customers by selling them things they supposedly cannot do without.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: desiderata are things wanted, not strictly essentials.
explanation.definitionFit: Desiderata, Latin for things desired, are items needed or wanted, close to necessities.

clue.text: Problem gripping Rex in a state

indicators.note: gripping holds firmly inside, so the problem word goes round the rest

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
R stands for Rex, king
taken as written

explanation.surface: A problem that grips a king while he is in a state of agitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a state' reads as agitated; state is the definition, a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Surinam, now Suriname, is a sovereign state on the north coast of South America.

clue.text: One church had to be decorated

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
CE is the Church of England
'd is the contracted form of had, as in I'd

explanation.surface: One church needed to be done up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decorated' here means covered with icing, as a cake is.
explanation.definitionFit: A cake that is iced has been decorated with a sugar coating, so iced is a specific kind of decorated.

clue.text: Drink? Church worker imbibes one — and another one

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the worker word takes a letter inside

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
I is the Roman numeral for one
the ant is the crossword's standard worker
a second Roman one

explanation.surface: A church worker drinks one glass and then has another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Imbibes' is apt for the drink but places the first I inside CHANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from Tuscany, an example of an alcoholic drink, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Bird losing tail, pinned down by wood and stone

indicators.note: losing its tail means the bird word drops its final letter
in a down clue, being pinned down by something means sitting underneath it, so the order is fixed top to bottom

parts.note: ash is a hardwood tree and its timber
the lark is a songbird

explanation.surface: A bird with no tail feathers is trapped beneath timber and rock.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'pinned down by' puts the bird below the wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashlar is squared, dressed building stone, or masonry made of such blocks.

clue.text: Projection of sentimental stuff suiting the nobs?

parts.note: corn is trite, sentimental material
U means upper class, acceptable to posh people

explanation.surface: Is sentimental slush really to the taste of the upper classes?
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old label for upper-class usage, as opposed to non-U; nobs is British slang for posh people.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornu is a horn-shaped projection in anatomy, the Latin for horn.

clue.text: A court beset by a hundred and one plants

indicators.note: something beset is surrounded on all sides, so the outer letters enclose it

parts.note: CT is the abbreviation for court
taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A courtyard overrun by a hundred and one plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Cacti, the plural of cactus, are spiny succulent plants of dry regions.

clue.text: What makes Oxford look bright?

parts.note: surface reading: something that makes the university city appear clever or cheerful
setter's reading: an Oxford is a style of laced leather shoe, given a gleam by polishing

explanation.walkthrough: Oxford wants to be the university, with bright meaning clever; it is a lace-up shoe, and bright means gleaming.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the polish applied to shoes, which leaves leather footwear such as an Oxford gleaming.

clue.text: Black farm building time's forgotten

indicators.note: something forgotten is left out, so the letter for time disappears

parts.note: a stable houses horses
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A black barn where time has been forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: Sable is the heraldic word for black.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is the heraldic term for the colour black, used also in poetry.

clue.text: Officer studies information schematically presented

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a table sets data out in rows and columns

explanation.surface: An officer pores over charts and diagrams.
explanation.definitionFit: A constable is a police officer of the lowest rank in Britain.

clue.text: Piece of cloth I found behind organ

parts.note: a lung is an organ of the body
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone finds a scrap of fabric behind a body part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' places I after the organ word.
explanation.definitionFit: A lungi is a length of cotton cloth wrapped round the waist, worn in South Asia.

clue.text: Duck is some swimmer, seriously!

indicators.note: some means only part, so the letters lie within the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: An admiring cry that a duck really is quite a swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck looks like the bird; it is the verb, to plunge under water.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck someone is to dip them under water, which is to immerse them.

clue.text: Hearing that is very irritating

definitions.meaning: first meaning: hearing a case in court, as a judge does
second meaning: annoying, testing one's patience

explanation.surface: A court hearing that proves deeply annoying.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge is trying a case when hearing it in court, and a trying person is wearisome and exasperating.
